objects.name: Sexton Rook
lines: Mind the soot, dear. I sweep round the outlines. Never over them.
Three alcoves, three statues, gone before anyone's grandmother was born. I still say good morning to them.

answer: Nobody remembers. The horde carried them out in the first year, like old furniture.
The soot kept their shapes, though. Soot's loyal like that.
...And a draught. And some nights, the smell of a candle. I don't go back there. I haven't the light for it.
The horde says it's a waste of a good roof. So it's quiet.
Quiet's a kind of prayer, if you let it be one.
Osric. Last of the Hales. The king we've got now was his younger brother, Kaldor.
Second born, and second best, his whole life, folk said. They said it quietly then. They say it quieter now.

questions.ask: You say good morning to soot? That's sad.
answer: The soot doesn't interrupt, dear. Or say things like that.
Good morning, by the way. I say it to everyone. Even you.
